notes: Planet Labs' first 10-K post-SPAC business combination with dMY IV (Dec 2021). Commercial Earth-observation satellite operator. Filing is light on named Pentagon Program Elements: revenue is described as a one-to-many subscription model, ~$131.2M FY22 revenue, with a generic 'Defense & Intelligence' vertical narrative and a U.S. federal-contracting subsidiary (Planet Labs Federal, Inc.) holding NISPOM facility security clearance. No specific PE numbers or named DoD programs (e.g., EnhancedView, EOCL, Tactical GEOINT) appear in the sliced 10-K. Closest J-Book-grounded surface is the 'high-value government procurement contracts', 'IDIQ / GSA-schedule' and 'Defense & Intelligence vertical' assertions. Carbon Mapper / NASA JPL partnership is civilian (NASA) — not DoD. Cohort prior at this 2022 cutoff: most relevant DoD commercial-EO procurement vehicles (NRO EOCL, NGA Luno A/B, JWCC, Project Maven imagery feed) were either not yet awarded to Planet as primes or not named in the filing — i.e., the company's federal narrative was still narrative, not booked-revenue concentration. ticker_pe_crosswalk shows 17 historical PL contracts (~$23.7M total, mostly Navy NIWC PlanetScope/EO subscriptions FY24-25) but ZERO matched against the J-Book PE corpus, consistent with PL being a commercial-data subscription vendor rather than a PE-funded prime. Control claims included for partnerships/facilities/counterparty disclosure.

claims.claim_text: Planet expects to continue to capture certain high-value government procurement contracts as a forward growth driver.
claims.subject: PL
claims.source_quote: the competitiveness of Planet's geospatial data set and analytic capabilities relative to other commercial entities and governments, including Planet's ability to continue to capture certain high-value government procurement contracts

claims.claim_text: Planet's Defense & Intelligence vertical is a major growth opportunity, with governments strategically engaging with commercial space and remote sensing companies to leverage sharable, unclassified subscription products to complement traditional defense and security industrial solutions.
claims.subject: PL
claims.source_quote: Defense & Intelligence: Governments are strategically engaging with commercial space and remote sensing companies to leverage sharable, unclassified subscription products to complement more traditional defense and security industrial solutions. In addition, we believe geo-mapping foundation data, maritime domain awareness, humanitarian and disaster recovery, and natural resource monitoring are examples of the many potential drivers of this opportunity.

claims.claim_text: Planet Labs Federal, Inc. is the U.S. federal-contracting subsidiary that holds NISPOM facility security clearance, a prerequisite to performing services requiring classified personnel for the U.S. government.
claims.subject: PL
claims.object_value: Planet Labs Federal, Inc. (NISPOM-cleared federal subsidiary)
claims.source_quote: We are subject to the requirements of the National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual for the facility security clearance of our subsidiary, Planet Labs Federal, Inc., which is a prerequisite to our ability to perform services requiring classified personnel for the U.S. government.

claims.claim_text: Planet has $131.2M of FY22 revenue (ended January 31, 2022), a base from which it expects to grow via federal, state, and local government customers alongside commercial verticals.

claims.claim_text: U.S. government customers increasingly procure via IDIQ contracts, GSA schedules, and other government-wide acquisition contracts — a procurement environment Planet operates in.
claims.subject: PL
